title: Mandate
description: What an agent may do for a principal, and on what terms. A user mandate is what a person consents to on the box's consent page: an agent may act for them, within these permissions and limits, for at most this long, with these calls approved one by one. A service mandate is what an owner gives a deployed agent that acts on its own. A grant is a mandate intersected with the agent's own permissions, never more. The mandate's name is the OAuth scope an agent requests to get it; the gateway lists the scopes a resource accepts in its protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728), so a standard MCP client finds them without configuration.

principal.description: user: the agent acts for a person who consented, and that person is the grant's sub. service: the agent acts for its owner on its own workload identity, and is the grant's sub itself.

open.description: Any registered agent may request this mandate, unverified ones included. Without it, only agents that list the mandate may.

consent.description: Terms of a user's consent. The text is what the consent page shows, in the user's words.

max_duration.description: Longest a consent may stand before the user is asked again.

ttl.description: Lifetime of one grant. Under a standing consent the agent gets a fresh grant when one expires; capped by the agent's max_ttl.

approval.description: Who approves this mandate's critical calls, and how. Without it, a critical call is refused.

required.description: How many distinct approvals. A user route needs exactly 1; a group route needs at least 2.

max_auth_age.description: An approver must have signed in this recently; an older session signs in again before voting.

expires_after.description: How long an approval request stays open.
